name: KZ Industrial
specialty: Heavy-duty labor frames, structural parts, industrial tools
slogan: Built for the job. Any job.
desc: Chinese industrial conglomerate dominating the Asian heavy labor mecha market. Docks, mining, construction — if it's heavy and needs to take punishment, it's KZ. Massively common in scrapyards because when a KZ breaks, nobody bothers fixing it. They just buy another one.
flavor: The paint's always peeling. The welds are always ugly. And the damn thing always works.
vendorLocation: Scrapyard salvage, Neon Bazaar bulk dealers
loreUnlock: Discover your first KZ part in the scrapyard.
notes: Also produces improvised fight weapons (d4-d6): industrial cutters, hydraulic rams, plasma torches repurposed from dockyard tools.

name: Sora Motor Corp
specialty: Mass-produced civilian frames and parts for transport and commuting
desc: The Toyota of mechas. Mass production, acceptable quality, affordable price. Everyone in New Tokyo has piloted a Sora — for delivery, commuting, short-haul transport. The Neon Bazaar is stacked with used Sora stock. They're what you buy when you need something now and can't wait for better loot.
flavor: Holographic Sora ads are everywhere. Smiling pilot, clean cockpit, zero scratches. Nobody's Sora actually looks like that.
vendorLocation: Neon Bazaar (always in stock), general market
loreUnlock: Purchase or salvage your first Sora part.
notes: Condition degrades faster than average (mass production = lower durability). Cheapest parts on the market. Ideal early-game filler.

name: Aegis-Tac Solutions
specialty: Law enforcement and corporate security frames, standardized patrol-grade equipment
desc: Multinational security contractor headquartered in Singapore. Supplies frames and equipment to New Tokyo police, corporate security, and private peacekeeping forces. Aegis-Tac isn't creative — it's consistent. Every part meets spec. Few surprises, fewer failures.
flavor: That 'Sufficient' in the slogan tells you everything about their engineering philosophy.
vendorLocation: Police Surplus (requires police reputation), combat loot from Corporate Security enemies
loreUnlock: Defeat your first Corporate Security Unit or reach Police rep 1.
notes: Condition degrades slower than average (mil-spec QA standards applied to police gear). The reliable B+ across the board. Also produces standardized short-category sidearms (tier 2-3).

name: Kuroda Heavy Industries
specialty: Military-grade frames, armor systems, heavy ordnance
slogan: Kuroda doesn't build mechas. Kuroda builds victories.
desc: The zaibatsu. Military-industrial titan with defense contracts across allied governments. Kuroda parts are what the player desires but can't afford until late-game. Everything is overengineered — stronger, heavier, more expensive. Maintenance costs reflect the premium.
flavor: The slogan appears on recruitment posters. It also appears on anti-war protest signs, dripping in red paint.
vendorLocation: Corporate Suppliers (requires military reputation), late-game mission loot
loreUnlock: Salvage your first military-origin part from a defeated enemy.
notes: Also produces tier 4-5 long-category weapons (competes with Valletta at the top end). Repair costs are ~30% higher than average due to proprietary components.

name: Phantom Works
specialty: Experimental tech, prototype systems, one-off custom builds
desc: Not a company. A network. Ex-corporate engineers who left (or were expelled from) the system. They operate from clandestine workshops and trade designs over encrypted mesh networks. Every Phantom piece is handmade — which means two 'identical' parts can have very different stats.
flavor: No logo. No manual. No warranty. Just a weld mark that looks like a ghost, if you know where to look.
vendorLocation: Exile Traders (requires Exile reputation), special events, unique mission rewards
loreUnlock: Make first contact with the Exile faction.
notes: statBias 'variance' means Phantom parts don't follow predictable stat curves. Each part is hand-designed with deliberate tradeoffs — e.g., a torso with 1 HP/turn regen but 0 armor, or legs with -30% weight but half normal integrity levels. The 'broken but brilliant' manufacturer.

name: Hayabusa Engineering
specialty: Custom lightweight frames, precision-tuned parts, artisan craftsmanship
desc: The protagonist's family workshop. Founded by Grandpa as a micro-operation building custom lightweight frames for racing pilots and freelance scouts. Never big. Never corporate. Grandpa was an artisan, not a businessman. The company died with him — but the blueprints, tools, and philosophy survived in the workshop. When the player crafts parts, they are literally refounding Hayabusa Engineering.
flavor: Every part stamped 'Hayabusa' carries the weight of three generations.
loreUnlock: Restore the Garage and discover Dad's Hayabusa Mk.I frame.
notes: All player-crafted parts and frames carry mfr: 'hayabusa_eng'. Stats are defined during crafting but inherit a slight condition_decay bonus (family quality). The starting frame (Hayabusa Mk.I) is the only non-crafted Hayabusa item — it's Dad's original build.

name: Daewon Dynamics
specialty: Electronics, sensors, neural interfaces, thermal management systems, backpack utilities
desc: The ambitious newcomer. Where Sora is yesterday's reliable Toyota, Daewon is tomorrow's Tesla-meets-Samsung. Specialized in electronics, sensors, neural interfaces, and cooling systems. They don't make full frames (yet), but their tech parts and backpack utilities are best-in-class. A Daewon torso runs cooler than anything else on the market.
flavor: Daewon's New Tokyo showroom is all white surfaces and blue LEDs. The contrast with the scrapyard outside is almost offensive.
vendorLocation: Neon Bazaar (premium section), market tech vendors
loreUnlock: Visit the Neon Bazaar premium tech district.
notes: Best heatMod in the game (negative = better cooling). Low HP and armor as tradeoff. Primary source of high-quality backpack utilities (Sensor Array, Stress Dampener, advanced cooling). Favors ENR/NEU-focused builds.

name: Shibata Arms
specialty: Firearms — machine guns, shotguns, SMGs, autocannons (short category)
slogan: When it absolutely needs to die.
desc: The most recognized name in mecha firearms. Machine guns, shotguns, SMGs, autocannons — if it fires a projectile, it's probably Shibata. Reliable, available everywhere, scaling from cheap d4 peashooters to premium d10 heavy autocannons. The 'default' arms dealer of New Tokyo.
flavor: That slogan is graffiti on half the walls in the scrapyard district. Shibata's marketing department claims they didn't start it. Nobody believes them.
vendorLocation: General market (tier 1-2), Police Surplus (tier 2-3), specialized dealers (tier 4)
notes: Weapons only — no structural parts or frames. Covers short category primarily. Above-average accuracy, baseline everything else. The gun that works every time. Existing weapons.json items: MG-206 'Rattler', Scatterblast SG-4.

name: Taeyang Forge
specialty: Melee weapons — heat blades, pile bunkers, chain swords, vibro-lances (fight category)
slogan: Forged in Seoul. Tempered in New Tokyo.
desc: Korean metallurgy meets cyberpunk energy engineering. Heat blades, pile bunkers, chain swords, vibro-lances — everything that cuts, pierces, or crushes up close. Taeyang weapons run hot. Very hot. High heat generation, but devastating damage output. The risk-reward melee specialist.
flavor: Every blade comes with a solar brand seared into the metal. Pilots say it glows faintly when the weapon overheats. Taeyang says that's a feature, not a defect.
vendorLocation: Neon Bazaar melee specialists (tier 1-2), Underground Contacts (tier 3-4)
loreUnlock: Acquire your first melee weapon beyond the Mech Fist.
notes: Weapons only — fight category. High baseDamage, high heatGen, low accuracy. Natural synergy with Light frames (fast heat dissipation offsets Taeyang's heat generation). Existing weapons.json items: ThermoEdge Mk.I, AP Lance 'Puncture'.

name: Valletta Precision
specialty: Artillery — missile pods, rail cannons, mortars, sniper systems (long category)
slogan: Distance is safety. Precision is mercy.
desc: Swiss-Maltese precision engineering applied to long-range destruction. Missile pods, rail cannons, mortars, sniper systems. Valletta is expensive, rare, and surgically efficient. Highest accuracy in the game, low heat generation, but supply costs are steep — precision ammunition doesn't come cheap.
flavor: Valletta workshops in New Tokyo are clinical white spaces that smell of clean metal. The staff wear lab coats, not coveralls. It feels more like a hospital than an armory.
loreUnlock: Unlock shoulder weapon slots (Medium or Heavy frame).
notes: Weapons only — long category. Opposite philosophy to Taeyang: cold, calculated, efficient. Natural synergy with Heavy frames (shoulder mounts + burst damage before heat accumulates). Existing weapons.json items: Valkyr Mk.I Salvo. Not available at tier 1 — minimum entry is tier 2.

name: Red Creek Arsenal
specialty: Cross-category weapons — copies, knockoffs, and occasional originals across all weapon types
desc: Not a factory. A network of workshops producing everything: Shibata copies, budget Taeyang knockoffs, discount Valletta imitations, and occasionally something completely original that nobody expected. Quality is inconsistent. Price is unbeatable. Always found in the Neon Bazaar.
flavor: No brand. No warranty. No questions. Every Red Creek workshop stamps its own mark — none of them match.
vendorLocation: Neon Bazaar black market (always in stock), Underground Contacts
loreUnlock: Browse the Neon Bazaar weapons stalls.
notes: Weapons across all categories (fight/short/long). Stats typically 10-15% below branded equivalents, BUT significantly cheaper and occasionally features a unique property (rare token effect, unusual stat combo). The 'let's see what happens' manufacturer. Max tier 3 — Red Creek can't replicate top-tier military tech.
